Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Aya Dataset: An Open-Access Collection for Multilingual Instruction Tuning (2402.06619v1) · paper method: The source’s Aya Dataset table reports 204,114 prompt/completion instances, comprising 138,844 original annotations and 65,270 re-annotations, across 65 languages classified as 22 high-resource, 12 mid-resource and 31 low-resource; these counts concern this paper’s dataset, not a separately inspected current artifact.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Aya Dataset: An Open-Access Collection for Multilingual Instruction Tuning (2402.06619v1) · paper method: The Aya Dataset includes all original annotations but releases re-annotations only when the summed character-level Levenshtein distance for prompt and completion is at least five; only languages with at least 50 contributions enter the final release.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Aya Dataset: An Open-Access Collection for Multilingual Instruction Tuning (2402.06619v1) · paper method: The paper warns that a few contributors dominate some languages, that the platform had no dedicated toxic/offensive-speech flags and no language-relabeling component, and that peer review does not guarantee every unsafe or misclassified example was removed.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Aya Dataset: An Open-Access Collection for Multilingual Instruction Tuning (2402.06619v1) · paper method: Aya connects original contributions, re-annotation and annotation-feedback tasks sequentially: original examples are reviewed in re-annotation, and re-annotations receive feedback; the leaderboard quality score averages reviewer ratings of a contributor’s examples.
